questions: Have you noticed any tightening or thickening of the skin on your hands or fingers?
Do your fingers change color (turn white, blue, or red) when exposed to cold or with stress?
Do you have difficulty swallowing solid foods or pills?
Do you have frequent heartburn or acid reflux?
Have you developed any new shortness of breath with daily activities?
Have you noticed any sores or ulcers on your fingertips?
Do you have pain or stiffness in your joints, especially in the morning?
Have you had any new skin changes or tightening on your face?
Have you unintentionally lost weight recently?
Do you have episodes of chest pain or pressure?
Do you have any problems with diarrhea, bloating, or alternating bowel habits?
Do you have dry eyes or dry mouth?
Have you noticed any swelling or puffiness in your hands or fingers?
Do you have any numbness or tingling in your fingers?
Do your symptoms get worse with cold weather?
orders: Full set of vital signs (BP in both arms, HR, RR, SpO2, temperature)
Inspection and palpation of the skin on the hands, face, and extremities for tightening, thickening, or telangiectasias
Auscultation of the heart for murmurs or pericardial rub
Auscultation of the lung bases for crackles
Comprehensive metabolic panel including creatinine and liver enzymes
ANA with reflex to specific antibodies including anti-centromere, anti-Scl-70, anti-RNA polymerase III, and anti-dsDNA
results: 1. Full set of vital signs (BP in both arms, HR, RR, SpO2, temperature)
2. Inspection and palpation of the skin on the hands, face, and extremities for tightening, thickening, or telangiectasias
skin examination: a painless, non-pruritic confluent erythematous rash on the left arm one day before the chorea began; it improved with doxycycline and clindamycin but the chorea did not
5. Auscultation of the heart for murmurs or pericardial rub
6. Auscultation of the lung bases for crackles
8. Comprehensive metabolic panel including creatinine and liver enzymes
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
10. ANA with reflex to specific antibodies including anti-centromere, anti-Scl-70, anti-RNA polymerase III, and anti-dsDNA
antinuclear antibodies and anti-dsDNA: ANA mildly positive at 1:40; anti-dsDNA normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Lyme neuroborreliosis with chorea (tick-borne *Borrelia burgdorferi* infection)

Alternatives:
1. Post-infectious autoimmune chorea (molecular mimicry triggered by the recent infection)
2. Sydenham chorea (group A streptococcal post-infectious chorea)
3. Drug-induced chorea (secondary to doxycycline or clindamycin)
